source_review.notes: Checked twelve primary sources: current OpenTelemetry trace, context-propagation, API, semantic-convention, sampling, and baggage documentation; current Apache Spark monitoring and scheduling documentation; Apache Flink metrics documentation; the Apache Hadoop MapReduce tutorial; current Dask performance-diagnosis documentation; and the original Dapper publication. Sources support span/link/context semantics, sampling limitations, engine event and metric correlation, scheduling and attempt lifecycles, performance diagnosis, and production tracing design. All twelve URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed run R, plan version P_k, stage S_i, logical task T_{i,j}, physical attempt A_{i,j,a}, and accepted output O_{i,j} as distinct identity domains.
Checked operation duration d(v), predecessor set pred(v), earliest finish F(v), critical path L, total attempt work W, failed work W_f, losing work W_l, and ready/admit/launch/end timestamps.
Verified that trace, span, parent, link, baggage, resource identity, queue, service, blocked, attempt, winner, and commit terminology remains consistent throughout.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical and physical identities are kept separate, and all durations and counts have explicit units or qualitative scope.

evidence: Executed batch-trace-critical-path with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced two winners, 16 seconds of map attempt work, 6 seconds of failed work, and a 32-second critical path.
Recomputed the compact example: admission 3, readiness 2, failed attempt 6, backoff 2, retry 5, shuffle 4, reduce 8, and commit 2 sum to 32 seconds on the controlling path.
Recomputed Exercise 3 as a 49-second critical path and 61 seconds of listed operation work, with the 12-second parallel map excluded from critical latency.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable fixture establishes deterministic local graph arithmetic only; it is not a cluster-engine or clock-synchronization simulation.

evidence: Checked F(v)=d(v)+max F(u) over predecessors with zero for source nodes and L=max_v F(v).
Verified the topological induction: every node waits for all predecessors, so its earliest feasible start is the greatest predecessor finish.
Confirmed W=sum_a d(A_a) sums physical attempt work independently of overlap and therefore is not interchangeable with critical-path latency.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The critical-path result is conditional on the captured dependency DAG and duration semantics; missing dependencies or timing gaps invalidate equality with observed elapsed time.

evidence: Reviewed empty predecessor sets, zero durations, parallel ties, high fan-out/fan-in, shared-service batching, nested overlap, and computed paths shorter than end-to-end elapsed time.
Reviewed retry storms, concurrent speculation, late losers, duplicate events, executor replacement, adaptive plan changes, corrupt shuffle blocks, and commit ambiguity.
Reviewed clock skew, negative derived latency, sampling before late failure, collector/export loss, truncation, expired UI history, and reconstruction from durable events.
Reviewed record-level span explosion, high-cardinality labels, sensitive SQL/paths/emails, cross-region propagation, excessive retention, and unauthorized detail activation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Absence, timing order, success, and completeness are all treated as evidence claims that can fail independently.

evidence: Traced run, code, configuration, input snapshot, physical plan version, stage, logical partition, attempt, resource, candidate artifact, accepted output, and committed generation identities end to end.
Checked every attempt has a unique identity and outcome while retries/speculation retain one logical task identity.
Checked atomic winner selection, committed-manifest evidence, late-attempt fencing, and exactly one accepted output per required logical partition.
Checked monotonic local duration, explicit readiness/admission/launch semantics, bounded attributes, visible sampling loss, and reconciliation with independent authoritative records.
invariant_checking.notes: Tracing observes protocol transitions; durable engine metadata and commit mechanisms remain the enforcing authorities.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from identity and lifecycle authority through propagation, interval semantics, relationships, fencing, accounting, completeness, reconciliation, and governance.
Checked the critical-path induction against a topological ordering and fan-in maximum rather than a sum of parallel predecessors.
Checked the attempt-fencing argument requires candidate identity, atomic acceptance, full logical-output coverage, and immutable committed metadata.

Reviewed counterexamples for trace-tree-as-DAG, one-span-per-task, longest-span bottleneck, summed-span latency, submission-based queue time, timestamp causality, worker-close success, and traces replacing event logs.
proof_review.notes: The chapter distinguishes mathematical consistency of a captured graph from empirical completeness and production protocol correctness.

evidence: Audited uses of causal, authoritative, complete, critical, accepted, exactly one, success, unique, durable, atomic, safe, and unbiased.
Confirmed the longest-path proof is explicitly conditional on the modeled DAG and duration semantics.
Confirmed output uniqueness is attributed to fencing and atomic commit protocol, while trace data is described only as supporting evidence.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No trace viewer, sampling scheme, or telemetry record is presented as universal proof of execution correctness.

evidence: Reviewed proposed measurements for planning, dependency wait, queue, launch, execution, blocking, spill, shuffle, retries, commit, cleanup, collector drops, and completeness.
Confirmed no universal span granularity, sampling rate, latency threshold, retention period, cardinality budget, clock accuracy, or collector topology is prescribed.
Checked failure-biased retention is not claimed to estimate population rates without known selection probabilities or independent metrics.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production thresholds and budgets require workload distributions, engine behavior, failure rates, telemetry capacity, security classification, and policy.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed traces as causal navigation across submission, planning, scheduling, task attempts, worker execution, shuffle, output commit, sampling, reconciliation, and governance. The chapter consistently separates logical structure, physical execution, resource identity, latency, work, and authoritative durable state.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed actionable identity schemas, readiness landmarks, propagation carriers, retry/speculation outcomes, shuffle-link scaling, commit evidence, clock handling, critical-path and work accounting, adaptive sampling, telemetry budgets, fixture validation, reconciliation, redaction, access, and retention. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from evidence questions and identity through lifecycle instrumentation, graph reasoning, operational trade-offs, misconceptions, and governance. Ten worked examples and five answered exercises cover interval decomposition, retries, critical paths, sampling, and sensitive telemetry.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external OpenTelemetry maintainer, Spark/Flink/Hadoop/Dask engine maintainer, distributed-tracing researcher, scheduler or storage specialist, reliability engineer, telemetry-platform operator, security/privacy/legal/records authority, affected-tenant reviewer, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
